calls.head: The Kraken shut down the dangerous stuff, the Canucks don’t
calls.body: On preventing dangerous shots, Seattle is one of the league’s best, but Vancouver is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should come at the Canucks’ net.
calls.call: The Kraken prevent dangerous shots better than the Canucks do.

calls.head: Bruisers vs. finesse
calls.body: The Canucks hit a lot, but the Kraken mostly don’t. Vancouver is near the top of the league for physicality, and Seattle is one of the worst. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Canucks.
calls.call: The Canucks hit more than the Kraken in the close stretches of the game.

surprises.head: Seattle’s power play feasted on Vancouver’s kill
surprises.body: Vancouver has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: Seattle’s power play created 14.1 expected goals per 60, against their usual 6.6 (about 7.9 against Vancouver) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Catton bags a hat trick
paras: Berkly Catton got the scoring started for the Kraken on the power play early in the first. Jake DeBrusk tied it up for Vancouver on the power play just under four minutes later, but the Canucks didn’t score again. Matty Beniers and Catton scored 54 seconds apart midway through the second to put the Kraken up 3-1. Jordan Eberle made it 4-1 on the power play midway through the third, and Catton completed his hat trick into the empty net with 43 seconds left. Catton’s goals came one on the power play, one at even strength and one into an empty net.

The Kraken drove the play, outshooting the Canucks 43-23 (33-14 at 5-on-5), and the scoreboard caught up. Philipp Grubauer made 22 saves for the Kraken, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 38 of 42 at the other end. The Kraken moved to 10-8-1 and climbed to fifth in the Pacific, while the Canucks dropped to 5-18-1, still last in the NHL.

items.text: The Kraken won for the first time in four games.
